newsitem.title: USA: Office Depot says slow PC sales hurt net.
newsitem.headline: Office Depot says slow PC sales hurt net.

text.p: Office Depot Inc said Tuesday that operating profits and earnings in 1996 were adversely affected by an increasingly sluggish computer market and significant price reductions in paper.
Operating profits for the year declined to $239,381,000 from $244,077,000 in 1995, while net income fell to $129,042,000 from $132,399,000.

But the company said that going forward, its investments in opening 66 new stores, adding major infrastructure in the Business Services Division and major upgrades and conversions in its MIS systems should result in increased sales.

The company also said that it expects to close on its previously announced merger with Staples Inc next month. The new combined company, Staples/Office Depot, will have more than 1,100 office superstore locations throughout the United States and Canada. This transaction is intended to be a tax-free exchange of shares pursuant to which the stockholders of Office Depot will receive 1.14 shares of Staples common stock for each outstanding share they own. The merger will be accounted for as a pooling of interests. The transaction is subject to the approval of the stockholders of both companies and required regulatory approvals.
